script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

Title: THE LOST SELF

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

JAMES, 35, a successful architect, sits alone in his dimly lit living room. He's lost in thought, staring at an old photograph of himself with his parents.

JAMES
(whispering)
I remember this day. I was so happy.

A tear rolls down his cheek as he remembers the past.

INT. CAFE - DAY

James enters a crowded café. He spots ANNA, 30, an old friend from college, sitting by herself at a table.

JAMES
(excited)
Anna! It's been so long!

ANNA
(surprised)
James! I barely recognize you.

They catch up on old times, laughing and reminiscing.

ANNA
You've changed, James. You've become...hollow.

JAMES
(defensive)
I've just been busy.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits on the couch, staring at the old photograph again. He looks lost, lost in his thoughts.

JAMES
(to himself)
I've lost myself. I've become someone I don't recognize.

INT. GYM - DAY

James enters the gym, determined to reclaim his lost self. He begins working out, pushing himself harder than ever before.

INT. ART GALLERY - NIGHT

James attends an art exhibition, seeking inspiration. He comes across a painting that catches his eye. It's a self-portrait of the artist, an elderly man, with wrinkles and bags under his eyes. But in his eyes, there's a spark, a light that radiates life and passion.

JAMES
(inspired)
That's it. I need to find that spark in myself.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - DAY

James begins painting, expressing his emotions on canvas. He pours himself into his art, allowing himself to feel again.

INT. CAFE - NIGHT

James meets with Anna again. He shows her his painting, explaining how it helped him rediscover himself.

ANNA
(teary-eyed)
I'm so proud of you, James.

JAMES
(smiling)
I'm proud of me too.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James sits in his living room, looking at the old photograph. But this time, he doesn't look lost or sad. He looks content, satisfied.

JAMES
(to himself)
I've found myself again.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
